issues.legal_issue: Separate statutory procedures for recovering tax arrears remain available unless the law makes one exclusive of the other.
material_facts: A business was assessed for sales tax and arrears remained unpaid.
Authorities first attempted recovery through a procedure treating the arrears as land revenue, but those proceedings were unsuccessful.
After the business’s partners were prosecuted for non-payment, a magistrate ordered recovery of the tax as though it were a fine and issued recovery warrants.
Authorities then resumed recovery through the land-revenue procedure, and the business challenged that procedure as unavailable after the prosecution.
issues.conclusion: The land-revenue recovery procedure and the procedure following prosecution were not mutually exclusive; the authorities could choose either remedy, and the later land-revenue recovery proceedings were available.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 13 and 19 of the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, one procedure allowed tax arrears to be recovered as land revenue, while the other allowed recovery of specified unpaid tax as a fine under the Code of Criminal Procedure, including section 386(1)(b). Where the law provides multiple remedies, one does not ordinarily exclude another unless the law says so expressly or by necessary implication. The Court approved Shankar Sahai v. Din Dial, I.L.R. (1889) 12 All. 409 (F.B.), 418.

rule.if: tax_arrears_recovery_case and distinct_recovery_remedies and not remedies_made_exclusive

predicates.tax_arrears_recovery_case: The proceeding concerns recovery of unpaid tax arrears.
predicates.distinct_recovery_remedies: The governing law provides more than one procedure by which the tax arrears may be recovered.
predicates.remedies_made_exclusive: The governing law expressly or by necessary implication makes one recovery procedure exclusive of the other.

issues.definition: When unpaid tax arrears are at issue, the law provides distinct recovery procedures, and it does not make either procedure exclusive, the authorities may choose either procedure.
